_note: The axes of the Latent Audio Synth (Crossmodal Lab), moved here from
gpu_service/services/cross_aesthetic_backend.py letter for letter in stage 6
of the move to ComfyUI. The DevServer
(routes/cross_aesthetic_routes.py) reads them, frames the neutral prompt and
the poles with the production frame, and hands the framed poles to the
package's node ai4artsed_audio_synth, which encodes them with Stable Audio 3's
text encoder and adds the pole directions to the base embedding.
semantic_axes: each axis is two text poles in the encoder's embedding space;
'd' is the cosine distance between the encoded poles (higher = more distinct),
'level' the register the axis names. 21 validated and one experimental.
pca_labels: the ear-validated principal components of the SA3 t5gemma PCA
(pca_components_sa3.pt, fitted on 392K prompt embeddings, [N, 768] unit
directions), each keyed by its explicit PC index so omitting one never
misaligns pcN -> component. Re-derived 2026-07-11. Naming is abstract
(texture), not content-literal, on purpose: the axis shifts timbre potently but
does not reproduce content. Each texture pair is grounded in the measured
acoustic contrast of the two poles (centroid=bright, zcr=rough, onset/s=dense,
rms=heavy); 'genesis' keeps the content origin visible. Dropped by ear: PC1,
PC6, PC9; PCs 11+ unvalidated.
production_frame: SA3's conventionalized TrackType frame for the axis
vocabulary (neutral + poles). t5gemma was trained on captions prefixed with a
TrackType tag; bare descriptors under-separate under it. Measured (the A3
screen, screen_semantic_axes_sa3.{py,md}): the typical drawbar's median
nrel_cos is 0.148 bare vs 0.291 'instrument'. Applied ONLY to the neutral and
the poles, so the axis directions (pole - neutral) are well separated (the
identical prefix tokens cancel in the difference). User base prompts are
deliberately NOT framed: a base is user content, not axis vocabulary.

pca_labels.genesis: sustained vs dense-rough-loud | engines vs laughter/applause/chatter
bright-crafted vs dense-wild | instrumental synth/funk vs wind/waves/birds
light vs dark-heavy-dense | cafe/canteen vs mechanical hum/vibration
dense vs sparse-clear | bird flocks vs a single man speaking
continuous vs broken-rough | rain/thunder/storm vs sheep/goats/frog
bright-sharp vs dark-full | percussive hit/tap/touch vs orchestra/trad. music
bright-light vs dark-heavy | shrill/harsh calls vs steady engine/vehicle idle
